[Sat 2026-05-09 09:01 UTC] Write the function to find every log file in the system's /var/log and attempt to compress them.

Add a function like this to your startup script (or a sourced `utils.sh`). It finds regular files under `/var/log` and tries to compress ones that aren’t already compressed (prefers `gzip`, falls back to `xz`), without failing the whole script if one file can’t be processed.

```bash
compress_var_logs() {
  local log_root="/var/log"

  # Require root (likely, for many /var/log files)
  if [[ "${EUID:-$(id -u)}" -ne 0 ]]; then
    echo "compress_var_logs: must run as root to read/write most of ${log_root}" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  # Pick an available compressor
  local compressor=""
  if command -v gzip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    compressor="gzip"
  elif command -v xz >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    compressor="xz"
  else
    echo "compress_var_logs: no compressor found (need gzip or xz)" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  # Find all regular files; skip already-compressed/common archive formats.
  # -print0 to safely handle weird filenames.
  find "$log_root" -xdev -type f -print0 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    case "$f" in
      *.gz|*.xz|*.bz2|*.zip|*.zst|*.tgz|*.txz|*.tbz2) continue ;;
    esac

    # Skip if not readable/writable (avoid noisy failures)
    [[ -r "$f" && -w "$f" ]] || continue

    # Best-effort compression; keep original metadata as much as practical.
    if [[ "$compressor" == "gzip" ]]; then
      gzip -f -9 -- "$f" 2>/dev/null || true
    else
      xz -f -9 -- "$f" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
  done
}
```

Usage (example):

```bash
compress_var_logs || true
```
